questions.learningObjective: evaluate reading flow in a design critique
questions.stem: On Reading flow: a designer reviewing a museum exhibition poster notices that a layout's elements are scattered with no clear sequence. What technique best establishes an order of reading?

options.text: Use scale, alignment, and repeated cues to guide the eye along a path
Make every element the same size so that the layout feels fair
options.misconception: confuses equality of elements with a guided sequence

options.text: Randomize the placement of elements to add more energy
options.misconception: mistakes uncontrolled randomness for a guided flow

options.text: Remove all contrast so that nothing competes for attention
options.misconception: eliminates the very cues that could guide the eye

questions.explanation: Reading flow is the path the eye follows through a composition. Designers control it with differences in scale, strong alignments, and repeated cues that create a sequence; scattered equal elements give the eye no route to follow.
questions.hint: How can placement and size tell a viewer what to read next?

questions.stem: On Reading flow: a designer reviewing a research institute's poster presentation notices that a layout's elements are scattered with no clear sequence. What technique best establishes an order of reading?

options.text: Use scale, alignment, and repeated cues to guide the eye along a path
Make every element the same size so that the layout feels fair
options.misconception: confuses equality of elements with a guided sequence

options.text: Randomize the placement of elements to add more energy
options.misconception: mistakes uncontrolled randomness for a guided flow

options.text: Remove all contrast so that nothing competes for attention
options.misconception: eliminates the very cues that could guide the eye

questions.learningObjective: evaluate rgb and cmyk models in a design critique
questions.stem: On RGB and CMYK models: a designer reviewing a museum exhibition poster notices that a design created with light-based colors prints with dull results. What best explains this mismatch?

options.text: Screens use additive light while print uses subtractive inks
Print can reproduce more colors than any screen can display
options.misconception: reverses the typical relationship between the two gamuts

options.text: The two models are exactly the same system under different names
options.misconception: denies a real and important distinction between the models

options.text: Monitors are unable to display any bright colors at all
